source.title: Probing the contents of semantic representations from text, behavior, and brain data using the psychNorms metabase
source.authors: Zak Hussain; Rui Mata; Ben R. Newell; Dirk U. Wulff

record.tranche_reason: The study measures representational similarity across text, behavior, and brain representations and reports that similarities are substantially lower across data types than within them. This bears on the incomplete-alignment aspect of V7, but it does not test convergence as models scale.
record.gate_note: The relevant results are the study's RSA similarities and same-data-type nearest-neighbor proportions in Section 4.1. The RCA probing and ensemble results concern prediction of psychological norms, not representational convergence. No model-size or capability sweep is reported.
record.test_reason: Within its own setting, the RSA in Section 4.1 bears on V7. Ten independently trained static text embeddings (fastText, GloVe, LexVec, CBOW and others, on varied corpora) align only moderately (text–text ρ̄=.41). Representations cluster by training data type, with only mild clustering by learning algorithm. This is a new setting (static word embeddings vs behavior- and brain-derived vectors), not a scale test. Brain and human-rating vectors are not models, so most cross-type rows do not bear on any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. Text, behavior and brain word representations encode systematically different information. Data type shapes representational similarity more than learning algorithm. Behavior representations capture unique affective, agentic and socio-moral variance and complement text.
record.recipe_differences: Uses RSA based on Spearman correlations between cosine-similarity matrices to compare word representations from text, behavior, and brain data. It does not reproduce a model-scale convergence experiment.

fits_no_version.finding: Text embeddings align more with brain-derived word vectors (ρ̄=.09) than behavior does with brain (.03). Brain–brain similarity is low (.12).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Model representations align weakly with neural recordings at the word level.

record.problems: The study does not vary model scale or capability, and reports no uncertainty estimates for the relevant RSA summaries. The brain representations have limited vocabularies, as discussed by the authors. The text's reported .97% text nearest-neighbor proportion is inconsistent with its description of that result as indicating high affinity.
record.rows_left_out: Section 4.2 and Figure 4 report norm-probing performance, and Section 4.3 and Figure 5 report ensemble norm-prediction results; these concern psychological-content prediction rather than convergence between representations.

untested.parts: No model-size or capability sweep; static embeddings only.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation test between representations.
No feature or circuit universality analysis.
Uses a single measure (RSA with Spearman and cosine) on one vocabulary; no metric or input variation.
No test of plateau with scale. Shared objectives are not isolated; only data type vs algorithm is contrasted qualitatively.

missing.what: Qualitative finding that representations cluster by data type and only mildly by learning algorithm, even where algorithms are shared across types (e.g. fastText CommonCrawl vs SGSoftMax Input SWOW). This is the key V7 data-cause evidence and has no row.
Per-pair Spearman similarities among the 10 text embeddings (e.g. same-algorithm vs different-corpus pairs), which would show the spread of text–text alignment.

record.verdict_notes: Only Section 4.1 bears on the claim. The text representations are static, pre-LLM embeddings, so the result says nothing about convergence in large models. No uncertainty is reported for the ρ̄ values. The '.97%' value is a likely typo for 97%.

versions.untested_parts: No scale or capability sweep and no test of alignment across independently trained models as size or performance increases.
No paired image-caption vision–language comparison or test of alignment as either model improves.
No comparison of same-architecture networks trained from different initializations, or analysis of shared features or subspaces.
No mapping, stitching, relative-representation, or unpaired alignment test.
No test for recurring interpretable features or circuits across models.
The study uses RSA on a restricted common vocabulary but does not compare similarity measures, settings, or input sets to test metric or data dependence.
The study reports cross- and within-data-type similarity, but does not test scaling, plateaus, or whether shared training data or objectives explain alignment.

rows.subject: text–brain representation pairs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: RSA: Spearman correlation between cosine-similarity matrices
rows.note: Aggregate across representation pairs; the authors describe considerable differences between brain and text representations.
rows.check: Text–brain compares models with brain recordings. No version names model–brain alignment.

rows.subject: text–behavior representation pairs (aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: RSA: Spearman correlation between cosine-similarity matrices
rows.note: Aggregate across representation pairs; the authors describe considerable differences between behavior and text representations.
rows.check: Text–behavior ρ̄=.20 vs text–text .41: different training data yields lower similarity despite shared algorithms, consistent with data explaining alignment. Caveat: the behavior group mixes trained embeddings (SGSoftMax, PPMI SVD, THINGS) with raw human-rating vectors. State should be observed, not partial.

rows.check: Ten independently trained text embeddings reach only ρ̄=.41, so alignment is far from complete. This is the core V7 row and should be main, not comparator. State should be observed.

rows.note: The text gives the value as .97% and describes the proportions as suggesting high affinity, especially for text and behavior; the stated value and description are difficult to reconcile.

relationships.condition: Static word embeddings trained on text corpora vs embeddings trained on behavioral data
relationships.reason: Text–text alignment is only moderate (r6, ρ̄=.41) and drops for text–behavior (r2, .20). The text reports clustering by data type with only mild clustering by algorithm, so training data rather than a shared model of reality drives similarity.
relationships.display_finding: Mean correlation was 0.41 between text embeddings and 0.20 between text and behavioral embeddings, with clustering mainly by data type and mildly by algorithm.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: Mean RSA similarities are lower across data types than within them, showing substantial data-type differences rather than complete alignment (r1–r6).
